correctness.rationale: Every binary palindrome is centered within a maximal letter run; a unique monochromatic palindrome must occupy an entire maximally long run, and a mixed unique palindrome is centered at the whole middle run. At most one candidate per run center for a fixed length. Disjoint center restrictions imply <=2 SUPSs when <=4 runs; with five runs <=3. The two separated centers 2,4 cannot simultaneously contribute shortest answers because the uniquely occurring 1 0^c 1 around run 3 is shorter. Three-answer words must use centers 1,2,3 up to symmetry; run inequalities force n>=14 with equality precisely 0^7 1 0^3 1 0^2 and its reversal/complement. The infinite W_{b,e} family has exactly three length-a answers with all shorter possibilities ruled out structurally. Independent exhaustive brute-force evaluated all intervals for all 1274 binary <=5-run words of lengths <=10 and the n14 canonical witness; source verifier also enumerates 6944 words up to14 but its logs alone are not a proof. All positions and factor multiplicities are understood occurrence-wise, one-based in theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The all-string alpha<=4 bound is weaker than alpha<=2/3 for restricted run counts and does not determine a minimal 3-answer length. Run-length algorithmic bounds parameterize m but do not show the exact three-answer threshold.
